articles.body: VR이 '보는 경험'을 다듬을수록, 약시 훈련의 설계 공간도 넓어진다 메타 퀘스트의 Horizon OS 2.10 PTC 업데이트가 화제입니다. 새로운 Theater 환경과 단순해진 Navigator 런처가 핵심인데, 요점은 하나입니다. VR에서 '콘텐츠를 보는 경험'이 훨씬 자연스러워지고 있다는 것. 엔지니어 관점에서 보면 이건 단순한 UI 개편이 아닙니다. 렌더링 파이프라인과 입력 계층이 정리되면서, 그 위에 얹히는 서드파티 앱의 설계 공간이 넓어졌다는 신호입니다. Theater 환경은 고정된 시청 거리와 앰비언트를 제공하고, Navigator는 앱 진입 마찰을 줄입니다. 즉 '몰입해서 오래 보는' 상태를 플랫폼이 기본값으로 만들어준 셈이죠. 훈련 앱 입장에서는 세션 지속 시간과 주의 집중이라는 두 변수를 플랫폼에 위임할 수 있게 됩니다. 이 변화가 유독 반가운 사람들이 있습니다. 약시(amblyopia, lazy eye)로 양안 협응과 깊이 지각 훈련을 해온 사람들입니다. 지금까지 이 훈련은 별도의 검사실, 불편한 패치, 그리고 지루한 반복 과제를 뜻했습니다. 콘텐츠를 보는 시간과 눈을 훈련하는 시간은 철저히 분리되어 있었죠. Seven Sports가 만든 Amblyotube는 그 분리를 없애는 접근입니다. Meta Quest 앱으로, 시청하는 YouTube 스타일 콘텐츠를 눈마다 다른 시각 경험으로 재구성합니다.

articles.title: Text Blaze Alternative: TypeCrux vs Text Blaze Compared
articles.excerpt: TypeCrux and Text Blaze do the same basic job: you type a short trigger, and a longer block of text appears in whatever field you are typing in. Both run as Chrome extensions, both support dynamic con…
articles.body: TypeCrux and Text Blaze do the same basic job: you type a short trigger, and a longer block of text appears in whatever field you are typing in. Both run as Chrome extensions, both support dynamic content like dates, forms and formulas, and both offer a free plan. The real difference is not the feature list. It is where your snippets live . Text Blaze is built around a cloud account: your snippets are stored on Text Blaze's servers and sync to that account. TypeCrux is local-first: your snippet library lives in Chrome's local storage on your own device, with no account and no server. Almost every other difference in this comparison — privacy, pricing, offline behavior, team sharing, cross-device sync — follows from that one design decision.

articles.title: What is agentic RAG?
articles.excerpt: What the interviewer is testing Whether you can distinguish agentic retrieval from a fixed pipeline and explain its benefits, costs, and production controls. Agentic RAG replaces one fixed retrieve-th…
articles.body: What the interviewer is testing Whether you can distinguish agentic retrieval from a fixed pipeline and explain its benefits, costs, and production controls. Answer framework Agentic RAG replaces one fixed retrieve-then-generate pass with a model-controlled retrieval loop. The model decides when and what to search and can issue several queries during that loop. It reads the returned results and may search again when it still needs evidence. This supports multi-hop questions, but it can increase cost and make evaluation harder. Cap the number of steps and log each retrieval so the decision path can be inspected. Sample answer I would define agentic RAG as a retrieval-augmented generation system where the model controls part of the retrieval loop.

articles.title: Cekura vs. Netra: Which Voice Agent Platform for Your Failures?
articles.excerpt: Voice agents fail in ways a transcript cannot show. A reply lands two seconds late. An agent mispronounces a name. A caller gets cut off, and the agent continues speaking. Teams that test only the tex…
articles.body: Voice agents fail in ways a transcript cannot show. A reply lands two seconds late. An agent mispronounces a name. A caller gets cut off, and the agent continues speaking. Teams that test only the text miss all of this, and then hear about it when customers start raising tickets with your customer support. Platforms exist to detect these failures before and after launch, such as Netra and Cekura. They both do simulated calls and scoring of production traffic. They differ in what they publish, where they go deep, and who each one fits best. Here's what I could verify, and where each platform excels. Start with the failure you need to fix There are three things most voice teams need. They need testing on the real callers they receive, accents and fast speakers and noise on the lines.

articles.title: Pydantic: Catch Bad Data Before It Reaches Your Database
articles.excerpt: A library lets members borrow books through a web form. One day, a member types -5 into the loan period field, another mistypes her email, and a third pastes an ISBN with a letter in it. The form save…
articles.body: A library lets members borrow books through a web form. One day, a member types -5 into the loan period field, another mistypes her email, and a third pastes an ISBN with a letter in it. The form saves all three loans without complaint. The reminder email bounces, the -5 loan shows as overdue, and nobody can find the book with the broken ISBN. The database stored what it was given. The problem is that nobody checked what was given first. That is the gap Pydantic fills. You describe the shape of the data once, as a Python class, and Pydantic checks every record against it before your code trusts it.

articles.title: A Privacy Tool That Interrupts Too Often Will Be Disabled at the Worst Time
articles.excerpt: Privacy protection can fail because it misses a secret. It can also fail because it covers so much ordinary content that the presenter turns it off. False positives are more than a cosmetic problem. I…
articles.body: Privacy protection can fail because it misses a secret. It can also fail because it covers so much ordinary content that the presenter turns it off. False positives are more than a cosmetic problem. If every order number, test value, and harmless identifier is hidden, the presenter starts pausing protection to finish routine work. The unsafe state becomes familiar. Then an actual API key, customer email, or financial value appears during a screen share. The goal is not to hide the largest possible amount of text. It is to keep protection useful enough that people leave it on. Start with the content that would create real harm List the values that should never be visible to the audience.

articles.body: For much of Avatar: The Last Airbender , waterbending seems like the most limited of the four elements for one practical reason: Its wielders need access to water. Firebenders generate their own flames. Earth is everywhere, and air is even more readily accessible. On her adventure with Aang, Katara is almost never separated from her water skin for this very reason. A waterbender in the desert is about as useful as a badgermole cub in a swimming pool.

articles.excerpt: Rediscover the groundbreaking sci-fi saga that changed action cinema forever, now streaming free on Pluto TV.
articles.body: Some science fiction franchises are so ambitious they become their own cinematic languages. Star Wars built an entire galaxy with a mythology that’s still growing almost 50 years later, while Blade Runner helped define the vision of a far-future Los Angeles through rampant tech advancement and unchecked capitalism. They’re the kinds of franchises that can change the way we imagine the future, influencing everything from fashion and technology to the stories other filmmakers want to tell. Plenty of franchises have tried to capture that same vibe, but few have managed to pull it off quite like The Matrix .

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. Here's why Venus Express mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this.

articles.title: Who is King Ghidorah? The cosmic connections of Godzilla Minus Zero's foe
articles.excerpt: Godzilla will go toe-to-toe with long-time foe King Ghidorah in Godzilla Minus Zero. This three-headed Kaiju's origins aren't just space-based; one of the largest structures in the universe shares its…
articles.body: Godzilla goes toe-to-toe with long-time foe King Ghidorah in Godzilla Minus Zero, which opened in theaters on Friday (Nov. 6). Though the three-headed golden Kaiju might seem like a natural native of Monster Island, King Ghidorah actually emerged from the depths of space. However, it isn't just the origins of King Ghidorah — also known as Monster Zero in the Godzilla movie Invasion of Astro-Monster (1965) — that are this beast's only cosmic connection. One of the largest structures in the universe, the King Ghidorah Supercluster , was named in honor of Godzilla's primary antagonist. Eat that, King Kong!

articles.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
articles.excerpt: By modeling how a planet without life develops its atmosphere, astronomers hope to be able to better distinguish rocky planets without life from those that are inhabited.
articles.body: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life.
